en.title: LAIKA's Wildwood Trailer Dazzles With Darkly Magical Animation
en.summary: The final trailer for LAIKA's adaptation of Colin Meloy's novel, Wildwood, has arrived, showcasing a breathtakingly animated journey into a hidden forest. Get ready for a sweeping, darkly magical adventure hitting theaters this fall.
en.body:
Prepare to be spellbound. The final trailer for **LAIKA**'s highly anticipated animated film, **Wildwood**, has officially dropped, and it is nothing short of a visual marvel. This glimpse into the Impassable Wilderness promises an adventure as breathtakingly beautiful as it is darkly enchanting.

Based on the celebrated novel by **Colin Meloy**, with illustrations by **Carson Ellis**, **Wildwood** plunges viewers into a world hidden just beyond the familiar. The story centers on the intrepid **Prue McKeel** (voiced by **Peyton Elizabeth Lee**), who bravely ventures into a forbidden forest to rescue her younger brother after he's abducted by a murder of crows. She's joined by her steadfast classmate, **Curtis Mehlberg** (voiced by **Jacob Tremblay**), as they navigate a realm teeming with talking animals, cunning bandits, and powerful figures driven by complex emotions. The film’s synopsis hints at a narrative that doesn't shy away from the story's deeper themes: "As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must find a way to save her brother while confronting forces that could determine Wildwood’s future."

Director **Travis Knight**, known for his masterful work on **LAIKA** films like **Coraline** and **Kubo and the Two Strings**, appears to have once again conjured a world that is both wondrous and perilous. The animation showcased in the trailer is a testament to **LAIKA**'s unparalleled artistry, with intricate character designs and richly detailed environments that invite exploration. The film looks to capture the immersive, sprawling nature of Meloy's novel, promising a cinematic experience that will resonate with both long-time fans and newcomers alike.

## A Feast for the Eyes and the Imagination

The trailers for **Wildwood** have consistently set a high bar for animated storytelling, and this final preview is no exception. The visual language employed is rich with detail, hinting at the complex ecosystem and the diverse inhabitants of the Impassable Wilderness. From the menacing crows to the fantastical creatures that populate the forest, each frame is crafted with evident care and passion. The film’s commitment to a "darkly magical" tone suggests a narrative that balances wonder with genuine stakes, a hallmark of **LAIKA**'s distinctive brand of storytelling.

## The Wildwood Community's Excitement Builds

Fans have been eagerly awaiting this adaptation since its announcement, drawn to the novel's unique blend of fantasy, adventure, and emotional depth. The release of the final trailer has only amplified this anticipation, sparking discussions across online forums and social media about the film's potential to be a new animated classic. The detailed world-building and the promise of a compelling narrative, as evidenced by the trailer, are precisely what readers of the novel have cherished, and the excitement for seeing it brought to life is palpable.

## What's Next

**Wildwood** is set to premiere in theaters on **October 23, 2026**. For those eager to dive deeper into the making of this animated masterpiece, details about the film's production are expected to be featured in the November '26 issue of Animation Magazine.

content_raw: News Wildwood The Final Trailer for Wildwood Is a Marvel of Animation If you go down in the woods today, you’re sure of a big surprise… By Molly Templeton | Published on September 16, 2026 Image: LAIKA Studios Comment 0 Share New Share Wildwood Is a Marvel of Animation&url= target=”_blank” title=”Twitter”> Wildwood Is a Marvel of Animation” target=”_blank” title=”Pinterest”> Image: LAIKA Studios I’m running out of things to say about how stunning the trailers for Laika’s Wildwood adaptation are. Based on the novel written by Colin Meloy (and illustrated by Carson Ellis), Wildwood is the story of a girl who follows her baby brother into the Impassable Wilderness after he’s abducted by a murder of crows. But it’s also the story of a woman whose grief leads her to make terrible choices, and of a forest full of magical creatures that do not all get along. Or, as the synopsis for the movie puts it: After her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) launches a desperate rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness — an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must find a way to save her brother while confronting forces that could determine Wildwood’s future. Wildwood , the novel, is long and complex and immersive; Wildwood , the movie, looks to be the same—and the filmmakers behind it are clearly not shying away from the heavier parts of the story. This final trailer leans into the battle at the end of the tale, and into the threat of creatures that wish to do Prue harm (or do they?). I don’t exactly know how writer Chris Butler ( ParaNorman ) and director Travis Knight ( Kubo and the Two Strings ) are going to fit the whole story in here, but they clearly know what the book is about. Knight told Empire , “The movie wanders, sometimes gently, sometimes not, through the long corridors of loss and grief; through the strange ways people carry what can’t be set down.” Along with Lee and Tremblay, the film stars the voices of Carey Mulligan ( An Education ), Mahershala Ali ( Moonlight ), Angela Bassett ( Strange Days ), Awkwafina ( Crazy Rich Asians ), Jake Johnson ( Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse ), Charlie Day ( Mythic Quest ), Amandla Stenberg ( The Acolyte ), Jemaine Clement ( Time Bandits ), Maya Erskine ( Mr. & Mrs. Smith ), Tantoo Cardinal ( Killers of the Flower Moon ), Tom Waits ( Seven Psychopaths ), and Richard E. Grant ( The Franchise ). Wildwood is in theaters on October 23rd.[end-mark] The post The Final Trailer for Wildwood Is a Marvel of Animation appeared first on Reactor .
